prompt:
Generate a single 1536x1024 landscape image: a flat, screenshot-like UI mockup of the first viewport of a marketing landing page for a product called Pemby. Match the attached reference image's visual world precisely — its palette, type weight and scale, pill buttons, layered soft-shadow cards, flat vector illustration and overall energy — but the content, the layout's right half and every claim are different, as specified below.

STRUCTURE:
1. The whole page sits as a white sheet with generous rounded corners on a near-black #0B0B0B background that shows as a band at the very top and the very bottom of the frame, exactly like the reference.
2. A nav row across the top of the white sheet: at the left a small circular black logo mark next to the wordmark 'Pemby' in heavy weight; in the middle four quiet text links 'How it works', 'Eligibility', 'Passes', 'About'; at the right a solid black fully-rounded pill button reading 'Drop your CV'.
3. The left half of the sheet, occupying about 48% of the width: a very large very heavy headline in near-black, sentence case, tightly leaded, reading on three lines: 'Only the jobs that can' / 'actually hire you.' — and inline immediately after the first line's last word, an outlined pill containing a long right arrow, exactly as the reference places it. Beneath the headline with generous space, a two-line subheading in warm grey at a comfortable size: 'Pemby checks who can legally pay you from your country, then sends only those roles. You apply yourself.' Beneath that, generous space, then a fully-rounded white pill input with a soft shadow, spanning most of the left column, containing the placeholder text 'Drop your CV — PDF or DOCX' at its left, a thin vertical divider, then 'Moldova' as a second field, and a solid black circular button at its right end containing a white upward arrow icon.
4. The right half of the sheet, about 52% of the width: a flat vector illustration of a confident young woman shown from the chest up in a yellow #FFC629 top with bold black outlines, holding a pair of binoculars up to her eyes with both hands — the same drawing language as the reference. Behind her, flat geometric colour blocks: a red #F03A3F square panel with a small white close-cross in its corner and a small yellow square inside it, and a blue #1B6BFF filled circle overlapping a thin outlined white circle.
5. Layered over the illustration's lower left, a white card with 24px radius and a soft wide shadow, tilted to no angle but offset so it overlaps the figure: its heading reads 'Today' in heavy weight, and beneath it two role rows, each row being a solid accent-coloured rounded square icon tile at the left followed by two lines of text. Row one: a green #17A35B tile, then 'Senior Frontend Engineer' in heavy weight and beneath it 'Hallow Systems · hires from Moldova' in warm grey. Row two: a yellow #FFC629 tile, then 'Staff Software Engineer' in heavy weight and beneath it 'Verdant Grid · hires from Moldova' in warm grey. At the bottom of the card, a quiet right-aligned text link 'See the reasons' with a long right arrow.
6. Overlapping the top right of that card, a second smaller white card with 24px radius and a soft shadow, standing higher in the stack: it carries a solid green #17A35B rounded square tile at its top, then the words 'Hires from your country' in heavy weight, then beneath in warm grey 'B2B contractor listed. Verified 4 hours ago.' No photograph, no avatar, no person in this card.
7. At the very bottom of the frame, across the near-black band, three items in a row, each a solid accent-coloured rounded square icon tile with a simple white line icon followed by two lines of white text — heavy first line, warm grey second line. Item one, yellow tile: 'Green, yellow, unclear' then 'Every verdict shows its reason'. Item two, red tile: 'Every 12 hours' then 'Open roles re-checked on the company board'. Item three, blue tile: 'Six ways of working' then 'Contractor, EOR, relocation, freelance, local, programmes'. These are facts about how the product works, never statistics.

THE WORLD — taken from the attached reference image, which is the binding visual reference. Match its
palette, its type weight and scale, its component shapes, its illustration style and its energy exactly.
Ground: pure white #FFFFFF. Ink: near-black #101010 for all primary text, #6E6E73 for secondary.
Accents, used as FLAT SATURATED FILLS and never as tints: yellow #FFC629, red #F03A3F, blue #1B6BFF,
plus green #17A35B. No gradients on any accent. No pastel versions of these.
Type: ONE heavy geometric grotesk with a large x-height, in the character of the reference's display
face. Display headings are very large, very heavy (800), tightly tracked and tightly leaded, sentence
case. Body is the same family at regular weight, comfortable size, warm grey. No serif anywhere. No
monospace anywhere.
Components, exactly as the reference draws them: fully-rounded black pill buttons with white text and
generous horizontal padding; a fully-rounded white pill input with a soft shadow and a solid black
circular icon button at its right end; white cards with a large 24px radius and a soft wide diffuse
shadow, LAYERED and OVERLAPPING each other at slight offsets rather than sitting in a neat grid; solid
accent-coloured rounded squares about 14px radius used as icon tiles with simple white line icons
inside them; an outlined pill containing a long right arrow.
Illustration: flat vector, bold confident black outlines, flat fills in the accent colours, with simple
geometric shapes — a circle, a square — sitting behind the figure as flat colour blocks. Friendly,
modern, confident. Never 3D, never gradient-shaded, never photographic, never isometric.
Energy: bold, high-contrast, confident and friendly. Lots of white space around very heavy type.

FORBIDDEN, non-negotiable, these break the product's binding rules:
No search bar. No job feed. No "Post a Job", no "Hire", no employer-facing anything — there are no
employer accounts. Never use the words: job board, recruiter, recruitment, placement, get hired,
guaranteed job, auto-apply, scrape, beat the ATS. No statistics of any kind — no member counts, no
company counts, no "people got hired", no percentages, no ratings, no stars, no testimonials, no press
logos. No real company logos or names of real companies. No avatars or photographs of people.
Also: no device frame, no browser chrome, no hands, no desk, no perspective, no tilt, no drop shadow
around the whole screen. The image IS the screen, edge to edge. All text crisp, correctly spelled and
rendered exactly as specified. No lorem ipsum, no invented extra text.
